capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare: 16.5 kWh battery (15.7 usable); Wikipedia lists 16.5 kWh for the Tesla ED2 pack without a label.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Green Cars Compare: "16.5 kWh battery (15.7 kWh usable)". CONFLICT: English Wikipedia (Smart Fortwo) says 14 kWh "initially" for the Tesla pack; 15.7 kept as the labelled usable figure.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: GUESS: Wikipedia says only lithium-ion pack provided by Tesla; Tesla cells of that era were NCA. No page states the cathode. Owner decision.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: GUESS: no page states the pack voltage; the 2017 pack has 96 cells in series (Wikipedia), about 350 V nominal, and the ED2/ED3 packs are assumed the same class. Owner decision.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare: no DC fast charging, and no battery-warming feature is described for the smart ED on any page opened.

ac_max_kw.notes: Green Cars Compare: AC up to 3.3 kW; Wikipedia (Smart electric drive): "has a 3.3 kW on-board charger" (ED2).

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare (ED2 page): "does not support DC fast charging"; other years assumed the same (EPA lists only 240 V charge times; the 2012 optional quick-charge announcement was for Europe).
